title: Drone pilot flashcards: for the FAA Part 107 remote pilot test
description: The FAA Remote Pilot (Part 107) knowledge test (UAG) as flashcards: the rules, airspace and charts, weather, loading, radio and airport operations, emergencies, decision-making, physiology and maintenance, each idea taught before it is tested. From 26 October 2026 the test adds image-based questions from current sectional charts (FAA Airman Testing Community Advisory, September 2026).
sourceShort: 14 CFR Part 107 and the FAA's handbooks
notice: Contains material from 14 CFR Part 107, FAA advisory circulars, the FAA Airman Certification Standards and FAA handbooks, which are US Government works in the public domain. This deck is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed or approved by the Federal Aviation Administration or the U.S. Department of Transportation.

changelog.notes: First draft, not yet released: awaiting the independent audit, a newcomer read-through and an expert review.
Removed a card that duplicated another card word for word.

glossary.ALC: course-number prefix on the FAA Safety Team website (e.g. ALC-451, ALC-677)
glossary.ASTM: ASTM International (a voluntary consensus standards body)
glossary.AV: altimeter and visibility (AWOS-AV reports altimeter and visibility)
glossary.CIG: ceiling (a tab on the Graphical Forecasts for Aviation)
glossary.PA: first letters of Alaskan weather station identifiers
glossary.PH: first letters of Hawaiian weather station identifiers
glossary.UAG: Unmanned Aircraft General – Small (the remote pilot knowledge test)
glossary.UGR: Unmanned Aircraft Recurrent (the former recurrent knowledge test)
glossary.VIS: visibility (a tab on the Graphical Forecasts for Aviation)
glossary.GGG: airport identifier (the part of KGGG after the K)
glossary.KGGG: station identifier used as an example in the Remote Pilot Study Guide
glossary.KJFK: station identifier in an FAA testing-supplement SPECI
glossary.KLAX: station identifier in an FAA testing-supplement METAR
glossary.KOKC: station identifier in an FAA testing-supplement TAF
glossary.IR206: an example IR (instrument route) military training route identifier
glossary.VR1207: an example VR (visual route) military training route identifier
glossary.BKN008: broken cloud layer with its base at 800 feet
glossary.OVC007: overcast cloud layer with its base at 700 feet
glossary.P6SM: visibility more than 6 statute miles (plus 6 SM)
glossary.R04: runway 04, the start of a runway visual range group
glossary.R17L: runway 17 left, the start of a runway visual range group

checks.what: Three independent audits read all 1357 cards against the current eCFR text of 14 CFR Part 107, AC 107-2A, the ACS, the Study Guide, the PHAK, the AIM and the testing supplement, for accuracy and for plain language, and checked every figure
checks.result: They found no card wrong. 7 unsupported claims, 12 ambiguous cards, 34 unclear ones and 125 minor issues were fixed; three chart crops were redone; 30 cards beyond the test's scope were kept as extra.
